# Jock

> Jock is a statically typed language that compiles to Nock (via the Nockasm
> intermediate form). Syntax is Swift-inspired first, Rust-inspired second;
> semantics are Nock-native: everything is a noun, functions are closures
> (cores at the ABI only), recursion is the loop primitive. Surface syntax is
> frozen for 1.0. Compiler and spec: https://github.com/sigilante/jock
> Site: https://jock.is

GENERATED by `tools/refgen.py` from the compiler and its corpus — channel `%rc`, commit `a1f9572`, 1154 vectors, 2026-10-30. Do not edit; regenerate.

This is the compact reference for a model writing or checking Jock. Every table below is projected from a normative spec and every refusal message is quoted from the compiler. The normative spec is `docs/spec/` in the repository; when this file and the spec disagree, **the spec wins**.

Longer prose, hand-written and not generated, is <https://jock.is/llms-guide.md>.

Each has a `.md` sibling that serves as raw text.

- [literals](https://jock.is/reference/literals/) — 15 literal forms, auras, 41 reserved type names
- [examples](https://jock.is/reference/examples/) — 38 complete programs with pinned values
- [transfer](https://jock.is/reference/transfer/) — 23 refusals that catch a habit from another language
- [tags](https://jock.is/reference/tags/) — all 202 refusals, 162 with a minimal program
- [absences](https://jock.is/reference/absences/) — 10 things Jock does not have
- [erasure](https://jock.is/reference/erasure/) — how types become nouns, and what sugar lowers to
- [abi](https://jock.is/reference/abi/) — 37 pinned arms, 22 prelude traits
- [machine](https://jock.is/reference/machine/) — the `--diag` JSON schema and exit codes
- [stdlib](https://jock.is/reference/stdlib/) — 9 library modules, 114 declarations, 96 pinned by a lane

## The standard library

Nothing below is ambient. A module arrives by name (`import hof;`) and the directory holding it must be on `--data-dir`. One page per module, one section per arm, each with the signature and the assertion that pins it.

- [hof](https://jock.is/reference/stdlib/hof/) — higher-order functions over closures and List (18 declarations, 18 pinned)
- [http](https://jock.is/reference/stdlib/http/) — the NockApp http driver, from the Jock side (22 declarations, 13 pinned)
- [interval](https://jock.is/reference/stdlib/interval/) — interval arithmetic over exact rationals (4 declarations, 3 pinned)
- [nockapp](https://jock.is/reference/stdlib/nockapp/) — the NockApp host's own effect vocabulary (1 declaration, 1 pinned)
- [parser](https://jock.is/reference/stdlib/parser/) — parser combinators (38 declarations, 33 pinned)
- [rand](https://jock.is/reference/stdlib/rand/) — deterministic pseudo-random numbers (12 declarations, 10 pinned)
- [rational](https://jock.is/reference/stdlib/rational/) — exact rational arithmetic over Int (9 declarations, 9 pinned)
- [twoc](https://jock.is/reference/stdlib/twoc/) — two's-complement signed integers at arbitrary bit width (8 declarations, 7 pinned)
- [urbit](https://jock.is/reference/stdlib/urbit/) — Urbit-native conversions, in Jock (2 declarations, 2 pinned)

## The specs

The six normative documents, mirrored with an anchor on every rule: <https://jock.is/spec/>. Every rule id above is a link into the rule that states it. Where a page here and a spec disagree, the spec is right.

- language.md <https://jock.is/spec/language.md> — surface syntax
- types.md <https://jock.is/spec/types.md> — the judgments and the type lattice
- runtime.md <https://jock.is/spec/runtime.md> — the pinned ABI, the Kernel trait, scry
- nockasm.md <https://jock.is/spec/nockasm.md> and nockasm-target.md <https://jock.is/spec/nockasm-target.md> — the IR and its conformance law
- chain.md <https://jock.is/spec/chain.md> — the nockchain interop surface

## The book’s back matter

The same checked facts in the book’s R1–R11 ordering, for a human reader rather than a retrieval layer: <https://jock.is/book/>. An agent wants the pages above, not these — they carry nothing the reference does not, except R5 (the guard set), R9 (a glossary indexing each term to the rule that introduces it), R10 (the examples as exercises) and R11 (where Jock deliberately differs from Hoon), which have no Rendering A page.

4 modules in the library are NOT documented: `chainkey`, `chainrand`, `chaintx`, `wallet`. Each targets nockchain and each interface is half of a contract with a driver this project does not own. They compile; there is no page for them.

## Rules a model gets wrong

The compiler carries 23 refusals whose whole job is to catch a habit from another language. Each line is the tag and the compiler’s own correction, quoted.

- `%decl-fond` — this type contains itself with no base case, so it has no smallest value
- `%decl-fond-deep` — this type nests deeper than the checker unrolls (64); it may be well-founded
- `%decl-fond-order` — the FIRST case of this union contains it, so the bunt diverges;  a non-recursive case must come first --- reorder the cases
- `%decl-indiscriminable` — this declaration holds a union whose members are not told apart by their nouns
- `%elab-too-large` — this alias elaborates to more nodes than a type may hold; aliases expand inline at every use
- `%kernel-trait` — the class must impl Kernel<E> or FullKernel<E>, naming its effect type
- `%lex-connective` — && is not Jock; the connectives are words: a and b, a or b, not a (bitwise is hoon.dis/con/mix)
- `%mint-call-arity` — call supplies no arguments;  this one takes some
- `%mint-cast-sealed` — a class is constructed only by the module that declares it; a cast would forge one
- `%mint-cast-sint` — a cast reinterprets bits; sint(n) converts @ to Int
- `%mint-edit-sealed` — a class is written only by the module that declares it; ask it for an arm that rebuilds
- `%mint-patt-bare` — a bare name is a binding, never a case; write .name or Type.name to match the case
- `%mint-slit-sealed` — a class is constructed only by the module that declares it; use a constructor it exports
- `%mint-unblessed` — module is not on the blessed list; see vendor/BLESSED.txt
- `%mint-unblessed-scry` — the namespace is denied under --nockchain
- `%parse-lark-cmp` — p.>= is the lark p.> then =; write p.> >= 3 to compare, or p.> = 3 to assign
- `%parse-minus-glue` — write a - 1 to subtract; the glued and half-glued spellings are reserved
- `%parse-no-result` — a program ends in an EXPRESSION; this one ends after its last statement
- `%parse-not` — ! does not negate; write not e (! appears only in !=)
- `%parse-private` — private marks a declaration or a func; nothing else exports
- `%parse-private-impl` — an impl is a global fact scoped by reachability; it cannot be private
- `%parse-ternary` — no ternary ?: in Jock; if c { a } else { b } is an expression
- `%parse-unglued` — f (x) does not call f; write f(x) to call, or ; to sequence

## Operators, tightest first

`language.md` [L-107](/spec/language/#l-107); the table is the rule. Comparisons at 8 and 9 are NON-associative and must be parenthesized.

| Level | Operators | Assoc |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | postfix: glued call `(`, glued index `[`, field `.`, lark `.<` `.>`, axis `.+n` ([L-46](/spec/language/#l-46) to [L-51](/spec/language/#l-51), [L-98](/spec/language/#l-98) to [L-105](/spec/language/#l-105)) | left |
| 2 | `as`, `as?`, `as!` | left |
| 3 | `**` *(reserved — [L-112](/spec/language/#l-112))* | right |
| 4 | unary `-` *(reserved — [L-112](/spec/language/#l-112))* | — |
| 5 | `*` `/` `%` `×` `÷` `⊛` `∩` `⊗` `∘` `·` | left |
| 6 | `+` `-` (binary `-` is spaced — [L-109](/spec/language/#l-109)) `∪` `⊕` `⊖` `±` | left |
| 7 | `??` | right |
| 8 | `<` `>` `<=` `>=` `in` `∈` `⊂` `⊃` | none |
| 9 | `==` `!=` `===` `!==` | none |
| 10 | `not` | — |
| 11 | `and` | left |
| 12 | `xor` | left |
| 13 | `or` | left |

## Literal forms

`language.md` [L-77](/spec/language/#l-77); the `$jatom` mold must match it.

| Form | Aura | Example |
|---|---|---|
| decimal | `@` (number) | `42`, `1_024` — underscore grouping (OPEN-11); `.` is never a digit separator |
| hexadecimal | Hex | `0x2a` |
| signed | Int | `+42`, `-42` — ZigZag. Rules [L-6](/spec/language/#l-6) to [L-16](/spec/language/#l-16) below |
| float | Float64 (`@rd`) | `3.14` — digit-dot-digit, both sides required, ≤ 15 digits; rounding pinned `%n`, no mode surface. Float16/32/128 pend need |
| boolean | `Bool` (logical) | `true`, `false` — the beta `?` type spelling is retired (OPEN-2) |
| char/cord | chars | `'a'` |
| string | String | `"hello"` |
| term constant | (constant atom) | `%foo` — tag spellings match `[a-z][a-z0-9]*`; `%1` is the numeric constant 1 |
| date / span | Date / Span | unspecified — [L-78](/spec/language/#l-78) |
| path | Path | indicative `/a/b/c` — [L-78](/spec/language/#l-78) |
| interpolated string | String | `"x = {x}"`. Rules [L-26](/spec/language/#l-26) to [L-32](/spec/language/#l-32) below |
| list | List<T> | `[1, 2, 3]`, `[]` empty — KERNEL form, typed nominally: `List<join of widened elements>` (heterogeneous elements are a join error); `[]` stays sing-null, nesting into every `List<T>` by N13; against a wanted `List<T>` the elements check against `T` directly (at parameterized traits) |
| map | Map<K->V> | `[1 -> 100, 2 -> 200]` — brackets, told from a list by the arrow; `[->]` is the empty map |
| set | Set<T> | `Set<@>([1, 2, 3])` — CONSTRUCTED, not spelled; `Set<@>()` is empty |
| tuple | product | `(a, b, c)` |

## Aura names

`language.md` [L-97](/spec/language/#l-97); the utterable set, not the whole semantic aura vocabulary.

| Surface | `$jatom-type` | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `@`, `Atom` | `%$` | the any-aura atom (top of the aura order — the parser maps the surface spelling to `%$`) |
| `Nat` | `%number` | the aura a decimal **literal** carries, ordered *below* `Atom`. Every `Nat` is an `Atom`, so a signature written `@` takes one |
| `Bool` | `%logical` | `true` / `false`; beta `?` spelling retired (OPEN-2/17). The annotation resolves through the **boot alias**, not a bare parser mapping, so the `%loob` guard rides along |
| `Hex` | `%hex` |  |
| `Int` | `%sint` |  |
| `Float64`, `Float16`, `Float32`, `Float128` | `%real*` |  |
| `Byte` | `%chars` | one UTF-8 byte; resolves through the boot alias (the `%byte` guard rides along) |
| `UniChar` | `%chars` | one Unicode scalar, `0x0`–`0x10FFFF`. Shares `Byte`'s aura and refines it with a wider guard, so a `Byte` flows **into** a `UniChar` and a `UniChar` does not flow back. Nothing converts silently: a scalar is one-to-four bytes, so encoding is an explicit operation |
| `Date`, `Span` | `%date`, `%span` |  |
| `String`, `Path` | (jnoun) | noun types, not atoms |
| `*`, `Noun` | — | any noun (top) |
| `Base` | — | BasedAtom: atom < 2^64 − 2^32 + 1 (types.md [S3.4](/spec/types/#s3.4); OPEN-4 resolved) |

## Erasure

`types.md` [S10.1](/spec/types/#s10.1). Erasure is TOTAL: no runtime type information of any kind.

| τ | ⟦τ⟧ |
|---|---|
| `%atom a g` | atom (aura and guard erased) |
| `%sing a v` | the atom `v` |
| `%cell p q` | `[⟦p⟧ ⟦q⟧]` |
| `%face`, alias | transparent |
| `%ref` | ⟦unfolding⟧ (seals erased) |
| struct | right-nested tuple of fields, **declaration order**. A **one-field** struct erases to its field alone and is therefore atom-headed if the field is — which is what S6's struct-implies-cell caveat and chain.md [C-25](/spec/chain/#c-25) both turn on |
| union case, nullary | the tag's **cord** — `enum E { zebra, … }` gives `E.zebra` the atom `418.530.878.842`, not an index. Probed |
| union case, payload | `[tag ⟦payload⟧]` (payload tuple right-nested) |
| `%or` | the union of member shapes (discriminable by S6) |
| `T?` | `~` (= `0`) / `[~ v]` — Hoon unit |
| `List<T>` | null-terminated right-nested list |
| `Map<K->V>`, `Set<T>` | hoon-138 treap shape, `+mug`-ordered — ordering pinned per language version; changing the hash is a versioned break |
| `Bool` | `0` (true) / `1` (false) |
| `%gate` | closure per [S9.8](/spec/types/#s9.8) — opaque |
| `%var` | opaque |
| `%noun` | any noun; `%void` — no values |

## Deliberate absences

Absence is unguessable, so it is written down. 10 rules, each something ruled out that now refuses.

- **[L-174](/spec/language/#l-174)** Implicit composition of adjacent expressions is removed.
- **[L-175](/spec/language/#l-175)** Juxtaposition collections are removed.
- **[L-176](/spec/language/#l-176)** The `((` pseudo-token is gone
- **[L-177](/spec/language/#l-177)** Whitespace-blind postfix binding is rejected.
- **[L-178](/spec/language/#l-178)** The glyph connectives `&&`, `||` and `!` are absent
- **[L-179](/spec/language/#l-179)** The opcode surface forms `+()` and `?()` are cut
- **[L-180](/spec/language/#l-180)** The core algebra is not in the language.
- **[L-181](/spec/language/#l-181)** There are no TRAIT OBJECTS or existentials.
- **[L-182](/spec/language/#l-182)** There are no exceptions, nulls, inheritance or macros.
- **[L-183](/spec/language/#l-183)** Self-hosting constructs are post-1.0.

## Machine interface

`jockc.sh --diag` emits one JSON object per run; the schema is pinned by corpus vectors asserting the exact string. Exit `0` compiled, `1` refused or crashed (JSON still emitted), `2` usage error. Read `status`, not the exit code alone.

```json
{"status":"ok","type":"Nat"}
```

```json
{"status":"refused","tag":"mint-limb","line":1,"col":1,"module":null,"report":["refused: %mint-limb at 1:1","  1 | nope","    | ^","  hint: [ %mint-limb","            '`nope` is unbound: no binding, declaration, or import provides it; if it is a `func` declared below, only ADJACENT funcs see each other --- move them together'","            p=1","            q=1","          ]"]}
```
